claim: act_node executes multiple tool calls sequentially in a loop without idempotency or per-call checkpointing, causing earlier tools (including previously approved sensitive actions) to re-execute when a later tool triggers LangGraph interrupt().
evidence: In Agent-Core/agent_core/graph.py:2129-2299, act_node iterates over all tool_calls in the latest AIMessage and awaits execute_tool_with_guardrails(...) (line 2186), which calls langgraph.types.interrupt(payload) in Agent-Core/agent_core/guardrails.py:367 for SENSITIVE tools. When GraphInterrupt is raised (re-raised at line 2192), LangGraph discards the in-flight node state and, upon Command(resume=...), replays act_node from line 2110. Every tool_call preceding the interrupted call is invoked a second time via tool_obj.ainvoke(validated_args) because none of the side-effecting calls are wrapped in a LangGraph task or tracked across interrupt replay.
runtimeTrigger: The LLM emits two tool calls in one turn: either [edit_file('app.py', 'old', 'new'), bash_exec('rm -f temp.log')] or two SENSITIVE calls [send_email(...), bash_exec('rm -f temp.log')]. On first execution, call 0 runs its side effect (mutating app.py or interrupting and then sending the email on resume 1), and call 1 triggers GraphInterrupt. When the human approves call 1, LangGraph replays act_node from the top, re-executing call 0 (failing edit_file because 'old' was already replaced, duplicating bash_exec side effects, or sending the approved email twice).

claim: bash_exec HITL guardrail relies on a narrow regex denylist and defaults unmatched shell commands to SAFE, allowing destructive file deletion and outbound HTTP mutations without human approval.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/guardrails.py:132-147 checks bash_exec commands against only 10 regexes in DESTRUCTIVE_BASH_PATTERNS (lines 44-79) and returns safety_level='SAFE' for any non-matching command. Commands such as python3 -c file/directory removal or HTTP POST, find -delete, file truncation via redirection (> file), symlink creation (ln -s), curl -F/--form or -T uploads, or quoted/subshell forms bypass every regex and run automatically without invoking request_human_approval.
runtimeTrigger: A prompt-injected or erroneous agent call invokes bash_exec with a destructive or outbound-mutating command that omits the denylisted tokens (for example using python3 -c, find -delete, or curl -T/-F); classify_tool_call returns SAFE and execute_tool_with_guardrails executes the command immediately without triggering HITL approval.
